newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH LIFT GLOOM WITH CUP UPSET.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH LIFT GLOOM WITH CUP UPSET.

text.p: Middlesbrough lifted the gloom of their wretched season by pulling off a 2-1 upset win over Liverpool to reach the English League Cup semifinals on Wednesday.
They were joined in the last four by Wimbledon, the unfashionable London club who sustained their compelling form with a 2-0 quarter-final victory against first division Bolton Wanderers.
The night belonged essentially to Middlesbrough, 18th in the 20-team premier league, who brought rare joy to their fans by toppling the leaders with an effective tactical performance.
Middlesbrough's hustle and bustle style stifled injury-hit Liverpool's characteristic fluent passing game, and the home side seized the lead after 14 minutes.
A sloppy clearance by Liverpool goalkeeper David James allowed midfielder Craig Hignett to fasten onto the ball and drive it home.
Liverpool fell further behind after 27 minutes when defender Steve Vickers hammered the second goal from a corner by Hignett.

The visitors played with greater conviction in the second half and their England midfielder Steve McManaman reduced the deficit after 65 minutes, sliding in Czech forward Patrik Berger's low cross from the left.
That was the signal for Liverpool to launch a furious late assault but Middlesbrough clung onto their slender advantage.
Wimbledon took control at Bolton with two goals in the first 22 minutes, Nigerian striker Efan Ekoku getting the first in the third minute with a superb half volley.
Ekoku set up the second goal with a run from halfway and a pass on the edge of the box to Norwegian midfielder Oyvind Leonhardsen, who curled a magnificent shot high past goalkeeper Gavin Ward.
Bolton, having already ousted premier league Chelsea and Tottenham, produced a gritty second-half effort but never looked like claiming the scalp of a third London team.
Wimbledon have now been beaten just once in 22 outings.
